problem: Two designs each claimed part of the same surface. react-viewer's E5 rebuilds the single-pull-request narration view in React and names it Flight deck. review-flight-deck computes a merge order for the whole open pull-request set and gives its surface the same name. Shipping them apart means building the pull-request surface twice. The first build would go against the viewer E5 is about to replace, and the second when E5 lands. The name collision is a symptom. Someone planned one program as two.
why_now: Both source designs reached stage review independently, and neither had read the other. Neither design has any code yet, so merging them now throws nothing away. Waiting until one shipped would build review-flight-deck's ordering UI against a viewer already scheduled for replacement.
approach: cobuilder-viewer is one program with three surfaces: Work, FlightDeck, and Reference. The team authors it as TypeScript and React under plugins/artifact/viewer/src/, and Vite compiles it into the committed plugins/artifact/viewer/index.html, per ADR-0023 unchanged. FlightDeck replaces the Pull requests tab and carries two modes. Single-pull-request mode ships first, at parity with today's viewer. Multi-pull-request mode ships later in the same design. A reviewer selects open pull requests. A skill run or scheduled workflow then simulates candidate merge orders against the common ancestor with git merge-tree, and replays the best one or two. It commits the result as data, and the viewer only renders that data. ADR-0027 records this, merging and superseding ADR-0025 and ADR-0026. Each surface also gets a detailed static HTML prototype, built against this repository's own real bundle data. A reviewer approves that prototype before the surface's build epic starts. review-flight-deck already used this discipline twice for FlightDeck's multi-pull-request mode.

alternatives.option: Ship react-viewer and review-flight-deck as two designs, sequenced
alternatives.rejected_because: That order would build the ordering UI against the viewer E5 is about to replace, then rebuild it in React. Someone would also resolve the name collision twice, once informally now and once for real later.

alternatives.option: Recompute the merge order live in the browser, on demand
alternatives.rejected_because: A browser cannot run git. ADR-0001's content policy also blocks it from fetching the evidence. That constraint is hard, not a preference, and it carries forward unchanged from ADR-0025.

alternatives.option: A scheduled GitHub Action recomputes the plan and commits it
alternatives.rejected_because: Divergent exploration surfaced this option, and the challenge gate corrected it. review-flight-deck's own record already resolved automatic triggering as a scheduled skill run or a workflow, matching every other Odyssey mode. A GitHub Action would add CI infrastructure this family has never needed.

alternatives.option: A persistent, org-owned service computes the join index and the merge plan across every adopting repository
alternatives.rejected_because: Divergent exploration surfaced this option, and the critic pass flagged it as a trap. It discards the install-surface rule outright, because no plugin in this family ships an agent, a hook, or an MCP server. It also discards the per-repo bundle model that ADR-0016 and ADR-0017 already committed to.

alternatives.option: Three new top-level ledger line kinds: path-acceptance, bundle-merge, blocked-pr-decision
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-0019 fixed the ledger vocabulary at comment, reply, and state, deliberately. A proposal, an acceptance referencing it, and a post-merge actual result are three subtypes of state. A future reader then never meets an unrecognised top-level kind.

alternatives.option: OpenPullRequest as its own hand-copied type in the multi-pull-request epic
alternatives.rejected_because: A field renamed on one type and not the other compiles clean on both sides and drifts silently. One branded extension, defined once, makes the type checker refuse the drift instead.

alternatives.option: Build single-pull-request and multi-pull-request mode as one epic
alternatives.rejected_because: Multi-pull-request mode needs the typed data layer and the open-pull-request entity that single-pull-request mode does not. One epic means neither reaches parity before the other's risk lands on top of it.

alternatives.option: Keep ADR-0020 as decided: ordered parts under viewer/src/, concatenated by build_viewer.py, in plain JavaScript
alternatives.rejected_because: Carried from react-viewer's own record unchanged. It fixes file size and fixes nothing about state, and it cannot type the joins that ADR-0018 already computes.

alternatives.option: Two artefacts: a React application served locally, and a reduced single file for publishing
alternatives.rejected_because: Carried from react-viewer's own record unchanged. It splits the truth. ADR-0001 exists because the served file and the published file are the same file.

out_of_scope: any change to what the generation scripts write into the bundle
a new record type, a new join, or a schema version bump beyond OpenPullRequest
the diff view's own rendering, which the team ports as it stands
publishing a Notion target, which stays a reserved flag value
a team's own auto-merge rules, which this design reads but does not define
the runner's credentials and permissions, which sit in the adopting repository
who deletes integration branches after a path completes
risks: a contributor now needs Node and npm to change the viewer, which the repository has never required
a committed build artifact goes stale the moment somebody edits the output instead of the source
a byte-equal rebuild depends on a pinned toolchain, and a version drift makes the guard test fail for the wrong reason
the React runtime is inlined into every published Artifact, which spends part of the 16 MiB budget
the merged program is large enough to stall mid-rewrite, now that it carries eighteen epics

the ledger's proposal line must record the exact ancestor SHA and the per-step simulation inputs, or a later audit or replay has nothing to check itself against. Neither source design carried that schema work
referenced SHAs can fall to garbage collection between acceptance and audit time, and this design does not settle a retention story
a long pause between accepting a path and running it lets the integration branches drift from the default branch, which reintroduces the conflicts the path was ordered to avoid
testing: Each surface's build epic depends on its own prototype epic. E5 waits on E4, E7 on E6, and E9 on E8. A reviewer approves each prototype before its build epic starts, so no build epic rests on an uncommitted or partial prior prototype. Those prototype epics build on two earlier results. react-viewer's 2026-09-07 prototype proved the Work board's shape. review-flight-deck's spike ran against hindsight_fork, a real multi-author repository. Thirty open branches shared one true common ancestor, and 42.5 percent of pairwise merges conflicted. A greedy minimum-conflict order beat arrival order by roughly 40 percent on stop count. Neither result replaces the new prototype work. E2 carries the byte-equal rebuild test, and E16 measures a real published Artifact against the 16 MiB budget.
reviewer_focus: E1 ordering: the exporter seam must land before any bundled output, or publishing breaks silently
the spike inside E2, which settles two of the three abort conditions before the rest of the work depends on them
E3's OpenPullRequest declaration, which must exist before E11 consumes it, or the type-drift guarantee ADR-0027 makes has nothing to enforce
E12's classification of the three non-authored conflict shapes, which is the part of the design with the least prior art
E14's ledger schema for a merge-order proposal, which is new work neither source design specified in detail
ADR-0019's comment anchors under React, which remain unsettled and belong to E18
unknowns: whether Claude Artifacts renders a Mermaid block that React injects after page load, or whether the team needs a vendored runtime
whether Vite plus vite-plugin-singlefile produces a byte-identical file across two machines with the same lockfile and Node version
how large the inlined React runtime makes a published pull request that also carries scene art
whether the viewer's anchored-comments ledger (ADR-0019) survives a React re-render
which ancestor to simulate from when several are valid for a disjoint or non-transitively-based open set, per Q1 and Q2 in the superseded review-flight-deck record
how many candidate paths to show before the choice becomes noise rather than evidence
what a team's own auto-merge rules look like in practice, since the split this design reads stays invented until somebody observes a real set of rules
the exact byte-equality test that tells identical-content conflicts from a real disagreement, and its cost against always re-running the shared-file generator instead
